newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli workers keep up strike, Netanyahu firm.
newsitem.headline: Israeli workers keep up strike, Netanyahu firm.

text.p: Israeli workers staged a second day of strikes on Friday to protest planned cuts in government spending but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu blasted their action as unjustified and politically motivated.
The strike closed Haifa, Ashdod and Eilat ports, and disrupted telephone services across Israel.
Netanyahu told government ministers in their weekly meeting that the strike was politically motivated and unjustified, a spokesman said in a statement.

Ministers rebuffed the Histadrut labour federation's claim that the strike was planned to protest against budget cuts, saying clauses in the 1997 budget that would have hurt the poor had been removed.
"What we we have here is an irresponsible, politically motivated strike and we condemn it," the statement said.

Leaders of the labour federation said strikes were planned in other sectors in the coming days and threatened a general strike on Tuesday when parliament is due to vote on the government's 1997 budget.

The government's 1997 budget proposal includes seven billion shekels ($2.15 billion) in spending cuts and new taxes and other revenue measures that Netanyhau has said are necessary to rein in the deficit. Union leaders say the measures will erode workers' salaries.

On Thursday all outgoing flights were cancelled at Israel's international Ben Gurion airport as a result of the strike. Incoming flights were allowed to land but airport workers did not unload baggage. But on Friday the airport was functioning as usual.
The budget must be passed in parliament by the end of the month.
